findings.evidence: Generic `a:hover, a:focus { color: #00478f }` (0,1,1) overrides `.ontario-header__logo { color: white }` (0,1,0). Focused/hovered logo text 'Ontario' (27px bold) renders rgb(0,71,143) on rgb(26,26,26): 1.90:1, needs 3:1.
findings.userImpact: Keyboard and mouse users lose the site name the moment they focus or hover the logo; low-vision users cannot read it.
findings.fix: Add a scoped `.ontario-header__logo:hover, .ontario-header__logo:focus { color: var(--ontario-colour-white); }` (or yellow) so header link states keep >= 3:1 on black.

findings.evidence: At 320 CSS px the 636px table is not in a scroll container, so the column, h1, lead paragraph, and header all stretch to 663px (documentElement.scrollWidth 663).
findings.userImpact: Users zoomed to 400% must scroll horizontally to read every line of text on the page, not just the table.
findings.fix: Wrap the table in `<div role="region" aria-labelledby="requests-caption" tabindex="0">` with `overflow-x: auto` (new CSS class in ontario.css); give the caption `id="requests-caption"`. Keep `id="requests-table"`.

findings.evidence: After a server-side validation failure all four controls have no aria-describedby and the asp-validation-for spans have no id. The client path is fine only because jquery-validation-unobtrusive injects aria-describedby at runtime.
findings.userImpact: When JavaScript is off or the CDN scripts fail, screen reader users hear 'Full name, edit text' with no error, even though the page shows one.
findings.fix: Apply the `aria-describedby-error` pattern: give each validation span `id="Input_X-error"` and set `aria-describedby` on the control (lines 35, 41, 47, 55).

findings.evidence: aria-invalid is null on every invalid control in both the client and server error paths; invalid state is conveyed only by the red border and pink background of `.input-validation-error`.
findings.userImpact: Screen readers do not announce 'invalid entry' when users move through the fields.
findings.fix: Server: `aria-invalid="@(invalid ? "true" : null)"` from ModelState per the pattern catalog. Client: set and clear aria-invalid in jQuery Validate `highlight`/`unhighlight`.

findings.evidence: After a failed server-side POST: focus lands on BODY, the title stays 'New service request - Ontario Common Service Centre', and `asp-validation-summary="ModelOnly"` renders nothing for field errors.
findings.userImpact: Screen reader users hear the same page title as before and are not told the submission failed or how many fields need attention.
findings.fix: Apply the `error-summary` pattern (linked list of errors, tabindex=-1, focused on load) and the `document-title` pattern ('Error: ' prefix when ModelState is invalid).

findings.evidence: All four fields are [Required] on the model, but no label, instruction, `required`, or `aria-required` tells users so before they submit.
findings.userImpact: Users only learn fields are mandatory after a failed submission.
findings.fix: Add '(required)' to each label per the ODS flag convention (or one 'All fields are required.' instruction above the form) and `aria-required="true"` on each control.
findings.notes: Wording follows the catalog's `required-fields` pattern; flag for content review.

findings.evidence: Focus ring is a 2.67px #ffd027 outline on white (1.47:1); the accompanying border change #333333 -> #0066cc differs by only 2.27:1. Neither cue reaches 3:1.
findings.userImpact: Low-vision keyboard users struggle to see which form field has focus.
findings.fix: Use the catalog `focus-visible` pattern: dark 3px ring (`--ontario-colour-black`) with the yellow kept as an outer halo.
findings.notes: Keeps the ODS yellow as a halo, so no new brand colour is introduced. Screenshot: evidence/focus-input.png

findings.evidence: At 320 CSS px the unbroken request ID in `<code>` extends to 367px (scrollWidth 367).
findings.userImpact: Zoomed users must scroll sideways to read the request ID they need to quote to support.

findings.evidence: The nav link matching the current page has no aria-current and no visual current-page style on any page.
findings.userImpact: Screen reader and sighted users cannot tell which section they are in from the navigation.

findings.evidence: After a successful submit the title is still 'New service request - Ontario Common Service Centre' and focus is on BODY.
findings.userImpact: Screen reader users are not told the request succeeded and must search for the reference number.
findings.fix: Apply the `status-message` pattern: title 'Request submitted', heading with tabindex=-1 focused on load.

findings.evidence: Two links named 'Privacy' go to different destinations: nav -> /Privacy (demo notice, line 23); footer -> ontario.ca privacy statement (line 47).
findings.userImpact: In a screen reader links list both read 'Privacy' with no way to tell them apart.
findings.fix: Content decision: rename one link, e.g. footer 'Ontario.ca privacy statement' or nav 'Demo privacy notice'.
findings.notes: Landmark context (navigation vs contentinfo) may satisfy 2.4.4 'in context'; a human should pick the wording.
